ruleset.name: Controversial Rules
ruleset.description: This ruleset checks Rust style names under historical CamelCase rule ids. Types use PascalCase; functions, fields, parameters, and locals use snake_case. See docs/controversial.md.

rule.name: CamelCaseClassName
rule.message: The type {0} is not named in PascalCase.
rule.description: It is considered best practice to use PascalCase notation to name structs, enums, traits, and unions in Rust.

property.name: camelcase-abbreviations
property.description: Reject consecutive uppercase letters in type names (HTTP → Http).

rule.example: struct bad_name; // violation struct GoodName; // OK

rule.name: CamelCaseMethodName
rule.message: The method {0} is not named in snake_case.
rule.description: It is considered best practice to use snake_case notation to name functions and methods in Rust.

property.name: allow-underscore
property.description: Kept for phpmd XML parity; snake_case already allows underscores.

property.name: allow-underscore-test
property.description: Kept for phpmd XML parity; snake_case already allows underscores.

rule.name: CamelCasePropertyName
rule.message: The property {0} is not named in snake_case.
rule.description: It is considered best practice to use snake_case notation to name fields in Rust.

property.name: allow-underscore
property.description: Kept for phpmd XML parity; snake_case already allows underscores.

rule.name: CamelCaseParameterName
rule.message: The parameter {0} is not named in snake_case.
rule.description: It is considered best practice to use snake_case notation to name parameters in Rust.

property.name: allow-underscore
property.description: Kept for phpmd XML parity; snake_case already allows underscores.

rule.example: fn do_something(userName: &str) {} // violation fn do_something(user_name: &str) {} // OK
